headline: PIMS Nursery Burned in One Minute
deck: Fourteen newborns died after an AC spark became a room fire in one minute, with oxygen accelerating the blaze. Families describe locked doors; PIMS says exits were open. A city report found fire safety inadequate and put the first brigade report at 06:55.

art.caption: Islamabad. CDA called the nursery’s fire-safety arrangements inadequate.

body: At 06:38 PKT on 26 August, CCTV showed a spark from an air-conditioning unit drop onto the floor of the PIMS Mother and Child nursery, Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal said. [E1] By 06:39, the whole room was on fire; PIMS’s preliminary account likewise said flames spread within seconds through oxygen points at each incubator. [E1] Oxygen accelerates combustion in an enriched environment, and the hospital said a huge blast and ceiling collapse followed by 06:39. [E1] Fourteen of the 15 newborns in the nursery died, with one baby rescued. [E1]

The CDA Fire Brigade Department recorded the blaze as reported at 06:55 and said its first engine reached PIMS within six minutes. [E2] That leaves a 16-minute interval between the room being engulfed at 06:39 and the fire being reported, before travel time is counted. [E1][E2] The same CDA account said firefighting and rescue faced significant obstacles. [E2] Six fire tenders and four ambulances ultimately took part, and authorities said the fire was brought under control. [E7]

Jaweria, the mother of one victim, told the BBC that the maternity-ward door was locked, while other witnesses described breaking through doors or windows to reach patients. [E3] Rescue sources separately said emergency evacuation routes were locked. [E2] PIMS answered later that all emergency exits were fully open and operational; its executive director told the BBC that security guards manned the ward door and denied it was locked. [E3][E4] Hospital officials said access had been restricted because of previous infant-theft incidents, placing a security control directly inside the inquiry’s egress questions. [E1][E2]

PIMS’s preliminary report said two doctors and two nurses were on duty inside the nursery and immediately called security, making two attempts to get babies out before the 06:39 blast. [E4] Kamal said CCTV showed the four medical staff running for help as flames spread. [E1] Families and witnesses said duty staff were absent; rescue sources likewise claimed no doctors, ward attendants or other staff were present in the incubation centre. [E2][E3] Those accounts conflict on who was physically at the nursery when ignition became a room fire. [E1][E2][E3][E4]

CDA’s Fire Brigade Department found PIMS’s fire-safety and life-protection arrangements inadequate and below prescribed standards. [E2] Kamal also acknowledged that the hospital had no sprinkler system. [E1] PIMS Executive Director Rana Imran Sikandar rejected the safety finding, saying the system was satisfactory and rescue teams faced no obstacles. [E2] The high-level inquiry’s terms of reference require a detailed review of PIMS fire-safety infrastructure and compliance with safety regulations. [E6]

Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif suspended Federal Health Secretary Aslam Ghouri and ordered his removal; Ghouri was also told to leave the emergency meeting. [E5] A high-level inquiry chaired by retired federal secretary Shahid Khan was ordered to establish the immediate cause and timeline, review the emergency response and newborn evacuation SOPs, inspect fire-safety infrastructure, and assign responsibility for negligence if found. [E6] That committee owes an interim report within 48 hours and a comprehensive report within five days. [E6] Separately, a seven-member district fact-finding committee headed by the additional deputy commissioner general was given 24 hours to examine cause, fire-safety measures, and rescue response. [E7]

Investigators now have three clocks to reconcile: ignition, egress and response. [E1][E2][E3][E4] The first is fixed at 06:38 for the spark and 06:39 for a room engulfed in flame. [E1] The second remains contested between locked-door testimony and PIMS’s statement that emergency exits were open. [E3][E4] The third begins with the fire brigade’s 06:55 report time. [E2] By the printed clocks, the nursery was engulfed at 06:39 and the blaze reached the fire brigade at 06:55. [E1][E2]
